issues.summary: Default 2 calls/10s global budget now governs positions, portfolio and wallet-portfolio as well as balances
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: configuration.ts:140-143 keeps the default of 2 per 10s, and the limiter now sits in front of positions (zerion-positions-api.service.ts:109), portfolio (zerion-portfolio-api.service.ts:122) and wallet-portfolio (:99). Any deployment still on the default will get new 429s on /positions and the portfolio route, and /v2/safes will mostly degrade. The PR description says tuning is left to ops, but the defaults it calls safe really do change behaviour.

issues.summary: Positions and portfolio specs stub assertWithinBudget as a no-op and never check that it is called
issues.label: medium
issues.evidence: zerion-positions-api.service.spec.ts:26 and zerion-portfolio-api.service.spec.ts:57 only define `assertWithinBudget: vi.fn()`, and neither file has a toHaveBeenCalled or LimitReachedError case. Removing the budget call from either service would leave every test green.

issues.summary: Per-address sub-budget is only enforced for wallet-portfolio; balances, collectibles, positions and portfolio pass no address
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: Only zerion-wallet-portfolio-api.service.ts:99-102 passes `address`. The balances (:136, :198), positions (:109) and portfolio (:122) calls omit it, so enabling the per-address config would not isolate a hot wallet on those routes, despite the class doc at lines 26-27. The tier is off by default, so this is low.

issues.summary: limitCalls=0 used to block every call and now disables the limit
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: The old check was `current > this.limitCalls`, which is always true for 0. The new check at zerion-rate-limiter.service.ts:92 is `if (this.limitCalls > 0)`, which skips enforcement. It is a real reversal of meaning, but a value of 0 is unlikely to be configured in practice.

issues.summary: ZERION_RATE_LIMIT_CALLS_BY_PERIOD description not updated for its wider scope or the 0-disables meaning
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: .env.sample.json:1576 still reads 'Maximum Zerion API calls per time period', while the new per-address entry at :1588 does document that 0 disables it. This is a documentation mismatch only.

issues.summary: A double failure logs the same error twice at warn level
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: serveDegradedBalance warns at safes.v2.service.ts:438-445 and rethrows, and the rejected overview is then warned again at :137-139. That is a small amount of duplicate log noise.

issues.summary: A successful degraded serve logs at warn level once per Safe
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: safes.v2.service.ts:429-435 warns every time the fallback succeeds, which is an expected outcome when the budget is exhausted. Under sustained over-budget this adds warn noise on top of the limiter's own warn at zerion-rate-limiter.service.ts:127.

issues.summary: The fail-open log is a plain string, unlike the structured RateLimit log in the same class
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: zerion-rate-limiter.service.ts:116-118 interpolates the error into a string, while _logRateLimited at :127-133 uses `{type: LogType.RateLimit, ...}`. Redis fail-open events therefore cannot be queried or alerted on by type or datasource.

issues.summary: The resolveChains doc comment describes the old per-entry drop behaviour
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: safes.v2.service.ts:182-184 says '(today the chain is fetched per entry)' and 'dropped during the per-entry build (as today)', but unresolved chains are now dropped in resolveSafes at :159-161. The comment is stale and misleading.

issues.summary: resolveZerionEligibility and resolveSafes run one after the other although they are independent
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: safes.v2.service.ts:84 and :88 are awaited in turn, and both depend only on chainsById. Running them with Promise.all would save one round of latency (feature-flag lookups against getSafe), a minor performance gain.

issues.summary: No test covers getChain failing, the resolveChains null path
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: Every getChain mock in safes.v2.service.spec.ts (lines 113, 142, 171, 200, ...) resolves successfully, so the catch at safes.v2.service.ts:194-198 and the drop at :160-161 are untested. The path is small, which keeps this low.

issues.summary: The ZodError and LimitReachedError logging branches are untested
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: The spec rejects getPortfolio only with plain Errors (safes.v2.service.spec.ts:203, :246), so the branches at safes.v2.service.ts:304-318 never run. The code is logging only, so behaviour is not at risk.

issues.summary: SafesV2Service calls the Zerion wallet-portfolio datasource directly instead of going through a repository
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: safes.v2.service.ts:60-61 injects IZerionWalletPortfolioApi, which goes against AGENTS.md ('Services ... call repositories (never datasources)'). The injection predates the PR, but the PR builds more logic on it at :268.

issues.summary: RateLimitGuard still uses increment, which relies on EXPIRE NX
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: rate-limit.guard.ts:35 calls cacheService.increment, which uses `expire(..., 'NX')` at redis.cache.service.ts:127, the same Redis 6 problem the PR documents. The file is outside the PR's changes, so this is at most low.

issues.summary: /v2/safes has no RateLimitGuard, so anonymous callers can drain the shared Zerion budget
issues.label: low
issues.evidence: safes.v2.controller.ts:73 has `@Get('safes')` with no guard. The route was already unguarded and previously hit Zerion without any limit; the PR only changes which counter gets consumed, and it degrades rather than failing.

issues.summary: The PortfolioResult 'degraded' variant behaves the same as a missing key
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: At safes.v2.service.ts:380-393 both a 'degraded' result and an undefined one fall through to serveDegradedBalance. The union is harmless and reads explicitly, so this is a style preference.

issues.summary: resolveZerionEligibility does not short-circuit when Zerion is disabled
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: When zerionBalancesEnabled is false, each chain returns false synchronously at safes.v2.service.ts:216-223 with no I/O, and fetchPortfoliosOncePerIdentity then finds no identities. The saving would be negligible.

issues.summary: The fake incrWithTtl duplicates increment
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: fake.cache.service.ts:82-87 copies the body at :72-80. This is a four-line test fake, so there is little real cost.

issues.summary: The fake incrWithTtl could be written more concisely
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: fake.cache.service.ts:82-87 is purely a stylistic simplification.

issues.summary: resolveChains builds an entries array before constructing the Map
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: `new Map(await Promise.all(...))` at safes.v2.service.ts:190-202 is idiomatic, so there is no concrete cost.

issues.summary: The interface doc mentions Redis 6/7 implementation details
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: cache.service.interface.ts:29-32 explains why to prefer incrWithTtl over increment, which is useful guidance for callers. This is a style preference.

issues.summary: The unit test and the integration test duplicate the 'one fetch per wallet' scenario
issues.label: nit
issues.evidence: safes.v2.service.spec.ts:107 and the integration spec both cover it, but the integration test also exercises the real wiring. Choosing between them is a test-strategy preference.
